body:
completeTicketOnIntegration (packages/fleet/lib/complete.mjs) detects a concurrent recorder sharing its ledger artifact via resolveManifestArtifactAfterWrite's line-count check (fixed this session for both the brand-new/pending-segment case and the already-open-segment case -- see this file's raced handling and its two regression tests). That check runs once, immediately after TicketService.apply's write, and is NOT covered by the manifest ledger lock. A concurrent recorder can therefore append AFTER the check returns raced:false but BEFORE this function's own git add / git commit stage the artifact -- the commit then captures both entries, and if the post-completion re-gate later fails, revertCompletionCommit sees the live ledger bytes match the committed blob (nothing changed SINCE the commit) and restores to the pre-commit state, deleting the concurrent recorder's entry along with the withdrawn one. Surfaced by a distinct-provider adversarial review (Codex) of PR #411 (T-MANIFEST-FOREST slice 3), round 4; confidence 0.99, HIGH severity. This is structurally the SAME class of problem assertOnBranch's own doc comment already names and defers (packages/fleet/lib/complete.mjs, 'NOTE ON THE RESIDUAL RACE': 'nothing we can lock stops an external process from running git checkout in a shared checkout... The complete fix is not to share the checkout at all -- give the integration branch a dedicated worktree. Tracked as follow-up.') -- generalized from git-ref races to ledger-content races in the same unlocked staging window. A real fix needs either holding the ledger lock across staging AND commit (a nontrivial redesign, since git operations run with the lock held, unlike every other locked section in this codebase which is pure filesystem I/O) or the dedicated-worktree redesign the existing comment already points at; neither is safe to rush into an already-large, already-hardened trust-root-tier PR.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A concurrent recorder appending in the window between the raced-detection check and git add/commit is detected -- either by re-checking immediately before staging while holding the ledger lock, or by eliminating the window entirely (dedicated integration-branch worktree). Verify: a new test that injects a recorder append at that exact point (mirroring this session's existing makeMidTransactionConcurrentRecorderGit injection technique, moved to fire between the write and the git add call) and proves the recorder's entry survives a subsequent failed re-gate and withdrawal.
2. The fix does not regress either of the two already-fixed race windows (brand-new segment, already-open segment) -- both existing regression tests in packages/fleet/test/complete.test.mjs stay green.
3. Full suite green: npm test.
title: Close the residual window between raced-detection and git staging in Fleet completion (T-MANIFEST-FOREST)
